This is really a philosophical question: humans are a part of nature, so, is what we do to/with nature also natural? I would say no. We have created things, devices, chemicals, and are even modifying DNA - in ways that have never existed before.

So onto the next point: over what time scale? Many of the things we have created will eventually revert back to their natural state, but it will take longer than my, my child's, and my grandchildren's lives to do so. I'll stick to that time-frame as a limit, so again no. We are changing the world in unprecedented ways and there will likely be serious consequences. Humanity has the ability to destroy all human life, but I doubt (even if we tried) that we could destroy all life on Earth. We might make ourselves extinct, along with many other species, but life on Earth will continue (within the aforementioned time-frame). I suspect humanity will continue to exist, even though we are meddling with the natural world. We are a clever species and seem to find solutions to the problems we create. It's really just a question of motivation.

I guess I wouldn't say it is facetious, maybe true with the caveat that natural and recycled isn't always "good." Everything comes from the earth and goes back to the earth, but many things can do a lot of harm in that process. Easy example- fossil fuels. Bit less obvious- plastics (from earth, recyclable, but not recyclable well... here's a quick explanation if anyone wants)

Also, we alter things that come from the earth in ways that would not naturally occur, and at a pace that it would not naturally occur at. I think this is the key to why this quote is a fallacy.
Its really a question of the definition of the words. Recycled, natural - they're not typically words that are well defined to begin with.
The distinction between "natural" and "artificial" always struck me as somewhat.... artificial.
I think everything is recycled because you can't beat entropy.

On a separate note: Greetings, everybody! For those of you who don't know, this is /v/Anime's first community viewing of Fate/Zero! Welcome!

In short, every other day I will be posting a discussion thread for an episode of Fate/Zero, wherein the community can discuss the show as we watch it together. At the end of each week, a thread will be posted that will serve both as a discussion of the current episode, as well as a discussion for all episodes viewed that week. I have two rules before we get started:

  1. NO SPOILERS

  2. NO HYPE

In other words, don't ruin the fun for anybody else. Spoiling is an obvious no-no, so use spoiler tags accordingly. By "no hype" I mean that comments shouldn't be made saying that the next episode is going to be awesome or whatnot. Doing this can raise people's expectations too high and ruin the experience. So, let's try to focus on the current and past episodes in our discussions, and use spoiler tags liberally.

As a side note, if anyone has any recommendations or concerns about any aspect of this viewing, please also voice them in these threads. This is my first time managing something like this and I'd like to make it as pleasant an experience as possible.

Episode title: The Summoning of Heroes

Database: [AniList] [Hummingbird] [MyAnimeList]
Stream: [Crunchyroll] [Netflix]

Note: Please do not discuss any plot points which haven't appeared in the anime yet. Try not to confirm or deny any theories. Minor spoilers are usually okay but still must be enclosed within a spoiler tag. Also, please refrain from hyping future episodes. It may ruin someone else's experience.

Should you have not watched Episode 1: beware, as there are spoilers ahead.
